newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates up on weekend cover.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates up on weekend cover.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates were slightly up on Tuesday as banks covered four days of weekend positions, traders said.
Money market trades were suspended on Monday due to floods in the capital.
The average rate rose to 18.0625 percent from 18.03125, with 31 lenders and 17 borrowers. Volume grew to 14.66 billion pesos from 12.35 billion.
Trading on the secondary market, meanwhile, was lacklustre as banks awaited for the results of the Treasury bill auction, traders said.
"Rates will fall but we don't know to what extent," a dealer said, since the market had been injected with two billion pesos of liquidity from maturing floating rate treasury notes.

"Most banks are not hard pressed to sell," another said. He projected the 91-day T-bill rate will not fall beyond 10.9 percent, the floor set by Central Bank based on its offer of special series T-bills.
A Reuters poll of five financial institutions gave bid rates of 11/11.20 percent and offers of 10.80/11.0 for the three-month bills.
